scope_note: Short independently rewritten revision items from publisher-labelled collections. The publisher describes the 2023 set as modelled; neither collection authenticates an official UTME sitting or paper order. Original reading passages, novel questions and doubtful keys are held. Source item numbers identify webpage positions only.
records: A runner trained hard but missed the marathon qualifying time by a whisker. Which statement is accurate?
She fell just short despite serious preparation
A whisker is a very small margin, so she narrowly failed to meet the target even after hard training.
The source contrasts arduous training with narrowly missing the time.
A detective found evidence underneath a dusty floor mat. Where was the evidence?
Underneath means below. The evidence was beneath the mat, not on top of it.
The source's detective finds a hidden clue beneath a rug.
Chika was reluctant at first but eventually accepted a difficult task and succeeded. What changed?
She was eager from the beginning
Reluctant means unwilling at first. Eventually accepting the task shows that she overcame that hesitation.
The source contrasts initial reluctance with eventual success.
A climber reached the summit despite a storm. Which account preserves both facts?
The storm made her turn back
She reached the top in bad weather
She climbed on a clear day
Summit means the top of a mountain, and despite shows that the storm did not prevent her arrival.
The source's hiker reaches a mountain summit despite stormy weather.
Which word is opposite in meaning to miserly when describing an employer's benefits?
Miserly means excessively unwilling to spend; generous describes a willingness to give.
The source tests the antonym of miserly in an employee-benefits context.
Which word is opposite in meaning to apathy toward public affairs?
Apathy is lack of interest or concern. Enthusiasm expresses active interest.
The source tests the antonym of apathy in a politics context.
Choose the opposite of incoherent in a description of a lecture.
An incoherent lecture is hard to follow; a clear lecture is understandable and well organised.
The source contrasts an incoherent lecture with clarity.
Choose the opposite of mundane when describing an artist's work.
Mundane suggests the ordinary or commonplace. Exceptional means unusually good or distinctive.
The source tests the antonym of mundane in a painting context; its source spelling is defective.
Which adjective is closest to effervescent when describing a lively personality?
Effervescent describes someone lively and cheerful; bubbly has the same figurative sense.
The source tests effervescent as a personality trait.
A pianist plays with dexterity. Which word best explains dexterity?
Dexterity is skill and ease in performing a task, especially one requiring controlled movement.
The source asks for dexterity in piano playing.
A company announces redundancies. Which word best describes the affected jobs?
In employment, redundancies mean jobs are eliminated and workers may be laid off.
The source tests redundancies in an employment context.
A film has a riveting story. What does riveting mean here?
A riveting story holds the audience's attention closely, so captivating is the nearest meaning.
The source tests riveting as a description of a film plot.
The new director has ___ the company's strategy. Choose the verb meaning changed.
Altered means changed. Alluded means referred indirectly; eluded means escaped; inferred means concluded from evidence.
The source selects altered for a change in company strategy.
The candidate gave ___ answers that stated the details plainly.
Explicit answers state matters clearly and directly. The other choices suggest avoidance or lack of clarity.
The source contrasts explicit interview answers with evasive or vague alternatives.
Because the pitch was unsafe, the team had to ___ the match and accept the loss.
To forfeit a match is to give up the right to compete in it, normally accepting a loss.
The source selects forfeit for abandoning a competition in adverse weather.
The coach's speech ___ the team's confidence before the final.
Bolstered means strengthened or supported. It fits a speech that increased confidence.
The source tests bolstered in a team-motivation sentence.
Learning idiomatic expressions ___ a student's command of English.
Enhances means improves. Learning expressions can improve command of the language.
The source tests enhances in an English-fluency context.
Which option has the same vowel sound as mine?
Mine and pint contain the /aɪ/ vowel. The other words use a short /ɪ/ sound.
The source compares the vowel in mine with pint and three short-i words.
Which word normally has its main stress on the second syllable?
Result is pronounced re-SULT. Taxi, famous and ratify normally stress their first syllables.
The source contrasts result with first-syllable-stressed words.
The principal bent over backwards to admit the learner. What did the principal do?
Bent over backwards is an idiom for making a great effort to help or achieve something.
The source tests the idiom bent over backwards in an admissions context.
The class had hardly entered when the bell rang. When did it ring?
Hardly had they entered when indicates that the bell rang almost immediately after their entry.
The source tests the sequence expressed by hardly ... when.
Our holiday plans fell through at the last moment. What happened to the plans?
They were delayed by one hour
A plan that falls through does not happen as intended; it fails.
The source tests fell through in a plans context.
After leaving prison, Bayo resolved to go straight. What did he resolve to do?
Go straight means stop committing crimes and live an honest life.
The source tests go straight after imprisonment.
With no fixed schedule, the organisers chose to play it by ear. What was their plan?
Play it by ear means decide what to do as a situation develops rather than follow a fixed plan.
The source tests play it by ear where the outcome is uncertain.
She completed the course ___ several setbacks.
Despite introduces a contrast: the setbacks did not stop her from completing the course.
The source tests despite before a noun phrase naming obstacles.
All the can directly modify the plural noun visitors. Each of would need a determiner such as the after of.
The source selects all the before a plural noun.
The insult felt like a slap ___ the face.
The established idiom is a slap in the face, meaning an insult or rejection.
The source tests the preposition in within the idiom slap in the face.
The grant will be divided between ___.
Between is a preposition, so its personal pronouns take object forms: us and them.
The source tests object pronouns after between.
The conductor, as well as her assistants, ___ at every rehearsal.
The singular subject conductor controls agreement; as well as her assistants does not make it plural.
The source tests singular agreement with as well as.
A compound number-plus-noun modifier before a noun is hyphenated and uses singular day: five-day programme.
The source tests five-day as a compound adjective.
My ___ is to read the instructions first.
Advice is the noun for a recommendation. Advise is the verb.
The source tests advice versus advise.
If an event is inevitable, it is ___.
Inevitable means certain to happen or impossible to avoid; unavoidable is the closest choice.
The source tests the synonym of inevitable.
The police hope to apprehend the suspect. What do they hope to do?
To apprehend a suspect is to arrest or capture that person. Charging and sentencing are later legal steps.
The source tests apprehend in a policing context.
A conspicuous mark is easy to ___.
Conspicuous means readily seen or noticed, so notice completes the meaning.
The source tests conspicuous in a birthmark context.
Which verb means to make an illness worse?
Exacerbate means make a problem or illness more severe; ameliorate means improve it.
The source tests the meaning of exacerbate in an illness context.
I cannot focus while the noise continues; it is a ___.
A distraction diverts attention from a task. Detraction concerns reducing value or worth.
The source tests distraction for something that prevents concentration.
Passengers are worried that bus ___ will increase next month.
The price a passenger pays to travel by bus is a fare.
The source tests fares for bus travel charges.
A country's representative who helps its citizens abroad is a ___.
A consul is an official representing a country abroad. Counsel is advice or a legal adviser.
The source tests consul in a diplomatic context.
Which spelling names a military or exploratory survey of an area?
Reconnaissance is the standard spelling for a preliminary survey or information-gathering mission.
The source tests the spelling of reconnaissance.
Which verb is opposite in meaning to intensify in the phrase 'intensify anxiety'?
Diminish means reduce; intensify means make greater or stronger.
The source contrasts increasing anxiety with diminishing it.
The peace agreement declared that there was no victor and no ___.
The vanquished are those defeated by a victor. The paired expression denies that either side won or lost.
The source tests victor and vanquished as opposites.
Her eagerness contrasted with her colleague's ___.
Eagerness is keen interest; indifference is lack of interest.
The source contrasts eagerness with indifference.
In 'AMINA bought the brown shoes', which question does the stressed word answer?
Stress on AMINA identifies the buyer, so the matching question asks who bought the shoes.
The source places emphatic stress on the subject of a sentence about shoes.
In 'It rained ALL day', which question does the stressed word answer?
For how long did it rain?
Stress on ALL identifies the duration as the part being corrected or supplied.
The source places emphatic stress on ALL in a rain-duration sentence.
Which word begins with the /j/ sound, as in yes?
Yam starts with the /j/ glide. The other words start with the affricate /dʒ/.
The source contrasts yam with words beginning /dʒ/.
Roam and home end in /əʊm/ (or /oʊm/), while loan ends in /n/.
The source asks for a rhyme with roam.
Bough and how share the /aʊ/ vowel and final sound.
The source asks for a rhyme with bough.
Rain and feign end in /eɪn/ despite their different spelling.
The source asks for a rhyme with rain.
Knight and cite both end in /aɪt/; their silent letters do not change that rhyme.
The source asks for a rhyme with knight.
Jeer and gear share the /ɪə/ ending in many British pronunciations; bear has a different vowel.
The source asks for a rhyme with jeer.

held_source_items.reason: Passage, register-cloze or prescribed-novel context is required; the public source does not establish reusable full-text rights or independent novel verification.
Duplicate or multiple viable options, unsupported stress marking, defective source answer, or missing underlining makes an unambiguous single-answer adaptation unsafe.
Passage or novel context, defective wording or answer, duplicate options, or a claim that needs more source reconciliation.
